chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, known as Ibn Maqbara al-Qazvini narrated to us; he said: Ubaydullah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Waqid in Baghdad narrated to us; he said: Isma'il ibn Musa narrated to us; he said: Sharik narrated to us, from Abi Rabi'a al-Ayadi, from Ibn Buraydah, from his father, that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:

Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, commanded me to love four people. We said: O Messenger of God, who are they? Name them to us. He said: Ali is one of them, and Salman, and Abu Dharr, and Miqdad. And He commanded me to love them, and informed me that He loves them.
ai.seo_question: Who are the four people the Prophet was commanded to love according to this hadith from al-Khisal?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Khisal highlights the divine command for the Prophet to love Ali, Salman, Abu Dharr, and Miqdad, reinforcing the concept of *Hubb al-A'imma* (love of the Imams) as a theological obligation. It underscores the unique spiritual status of these four figures, linking their love directly to God's own affection, a key theme in Shia exegesis regarding the Ahl al-Bayt and their close companions.
